“Sonali, why do you look down when Nanaji talks to you?” asked Saurabh, who had just moved to Delhi from Manchester.
“It's respect. Looking straight at elders can seem rude.”
“At my old school, looking down would mean you were hiding something.”
“That's silly! I'm not hiding anything.”
“I know, I know. I just think it's different.”
Nanaji laughed from his chair. “Both my grandchildren are honest, whichever way they look.”
Sonali looked up at him and smiled. Saurabh grinned.

"Look at me when you say that," said Mr Alvarez.

Mr Alvarez rubbed his chin. "And where I grew up, looking away meant lying. Maybe neither one means that."
